channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: The Lancet Warns of Nuclear War and AI Misuse Threatening Human Survival
item.description: The Lancet's latest assessment identifies nuclear war and the destructive use of artificial intelligence as the top threats to human survival by 2100. These risks, along with climate change and malnutrition, are interconnected and require simultaneous action. Experts emphasize that decisions made today will shape future generations' health.

item.title: UNESCO Initiates Efforts to Restore and Protect Afghanistan's Jam Minaret
item.description: UNESCO has launched initiatives to protect and restore the Minaret of Jam, a World Heritage site in Afghanistan. With ALIPH funding, measures are being taken to monitor its condition, mitigate flood risks, and ensure long-term preservation. Improved access via a new bridge facilitates emergency interventions and safer travel.

item.title: Taliban Evict Nangarhar Residents to Accommodate Associates of Red Crescent Head
item.description: Sources report that armed Taliban members have forcibly evicted residents from their homes in Nangarhar's Angor Bagh area to house individuals affiliated with Shahabuddin Delawar, head of the Taliban’s Red Crescent Authority. Protests by residents were suppressed by the Taliban.

item.title: Women Imprisoned in Taliban Jails Face Harsh Conditions and Vague Accusations
item.description: Hundreds of women have been imprisoned by the Taliban in Afghanistan over the past five years, often on vague charges or family disputes. An account from a former detainee details the harsh realities and painful experiences of women held in Kabul's Taliban-run prisons, highlighting issues of 'moral corruption' accusations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry of Labor Explains How to Appeal Disability Group Status
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection has outlined the procedure for appealing disability group status. Individuals disagreeing with the established group, duration, or cause of disability can file a complaint within three months. The process involves re-examination, including medical document review and patient assessment, potentially with specialist consultations.

item.title: inDrive Founder Comments on Soaring Ride Prices After Yandex Go Outage
item.description: inDrive founder Arsen Tomsky addressed a significant surge in ride prices on the platform, which users reported after Yandex Go services became unavailable. Tomsky acknowledged the imbalance between demand and supply due to increased passenger flow, stating the company is working to manage price increases and has reduced commissions.

item.title: Japan Plans Lunar Solar Ring to Transmit Electricity to Earth
item.description: Japan intends to construct a massive solar ring around the Moon to generate and transmit electricity to Earth. This project could eliminate the need for energy production from coal, oil, or biomass. Construction will be managed by robots controlled from Earth.

item.title: Kabul Women Entrepreneurs Face Business Decline Amid Poverty and Taliban Restrictions
item.description: Women entrepreneurs in Kabul report a significant slump in business due to rising raw material costs, decreased public purchasing power, and Taliban restrictions on women's activities. Many struggle to cover operational costs, leading some to reduce staff or halt production. They seek support, access to affordable materials, and exhibition opportunities.

item.title: Helmand Families Report Bread Collection by Madrasa Students as a Significant Burden
item.description: Residents in Helmand province, Afghanistan, report that madrasa students continue to collect bread from the public five years into Taliban rule. Despite allocated funds for madrasas, this practice, along with cash collections, places a heavy burden on impoverished families facing hunger and unemployment. Residents claim students, linked to the Taliban, humiliate those who refuse to provide food.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Economic Diplomacy Through International Engagements
item.description: Uzbekistan is actively enhancing its economic diplomacy, with embassies and consulates abroad facilitating engagements. Recent activities include discussions in Germany on consumer protection and competition, meetings in Oman concerning bilateral relations, a roundtable in France celebrating Amir Timur's legacy, and cultural cooperation talks in Hungary regarding jazz festivals.

item.title: UN Highlights Girls' Resilience in Pursuing Dreams Despite Global Barriers
item.description: The United Nations reports that girls worldwide are overcoming obstacles to achieve their aspirations. On the International Day of the Girl, the UN called for support, noting challenges like denied education, forced marriage, and gender-based violence. Despite these issues, girls continue to strive for their dreams.

item.title: UNFPA Afghanistan Calls for End to Child Marriage, Urges Investment in Girls' Rights
item.description: The UN Population Fund (UNFPA) in Afghanistan has urged an end to child marriage and called for investment in girls' rights on the International Day of the Girl. The agency warned that early pregnancy poses serious risks to young mothers, emphasizing that timely healthcare access can save lives and strengthen communities.

item.title: Uzbekistan and China Discuss Prospects for International Cooperation in Energy
item.description: Uzbekistan and China explored international cooperation in the energy sector, focusing on modern technologies and scientific developments. A meeting at Tashkent Chemical-Technological Institute's Yangiyer branch with Tianjin Agricultural University representatives discussed improving lithium-ion battery production technology and attracting investment.

item.title: UNESCO Warns Jam Minaret Faces Serious Threats from Natural Disasters and Conservation Challenges
item.description: UNESCO reports that the historic Jam Minaret in Ghor province, Afghanistan, is under serious threat due to natural disasters and conservation challenges, requiring urgent attention. The organization is undertaking monitoring, flood risk reduction, and local community support initiatives with financial backing. Regular data analysis aids in understanding the minaret's condition for long-term preservation.

item.title: Zelensky Sets Condition for Halting Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has reportedly set a condition for Ukrainian forces to cease drone attacks on Russian oil refineries. The specific condition was not disclosed in the provided text, but it is linked to a conversation with former US President Donald Trump. The context suggests a potential diplomatic negotiation regarding the conflict.

item.title: OSCE Facilitates Central Asian Border Security Training in Tashkent
item.description: The OSCE conducted a regional training course on detecting weapons, ammunition, and explosives in Tashkent. Fifteen border and customs officers from five Central Asian countries participated. The training focused on practical skills for identifying illegally transported firearms and explosives using service dogs, and harmonizing evaluation criteria for canine units.

item.title: At Least 109 Migrants Drown After Boat Capsizes Off Djibouti Coast
item.description: The International Organization for Migration reported that at least 109 migrants, including 15 children, died when their boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti. The vessel, carrying 350 people en route to Yemen, sank on October 8-9. Survivors, all Ethiopian nationals, stated the boat departed from Djibouti. Over 80 people survived, while more than 116 remain missing.

item.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's interim chief minister arrested amid state of emergency
item.description: Sohail Afredi, the interim chief minister of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, has been arrested. The arrest occurred after the federal government declared a state of emergency in the province, citing the provincial government's alleged deliberate withdrawal from counter-terrorism efforts. The Pakistani president confirmed the emergency declaration.

item.title: Zelensky responds to Trump's statements on Ukraine-Russia conflict
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine would cease striking Russian oil refineries if Russia stopped attacking Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Zelensky commented on recent US presidential statements, emphasizing that any de-escalation steps must be mutual and secured by concrete guarantees. Trump had accused Ukraine of exacerbating diesel shortages.

item.title: Finland Proposes Schengen Visa Ban for Russian Tourists Amid Security Concerns
item.description: Finland is proposing a ban on Schengen visas for Russian tourists, citing concerns over Russia's disruptive activities in Europe. The proposal will be discussed at an upcoming EU leaders' summit in Brussels. This move reflects growing tensions and security considerations within the European Union regarding Russian citizens' travel.

item.title: Afghanistan Signs Regional Trade and Investment Deals Worth Nearly $400 Million
item.description: Afghanistan has signed memorandums of understanding worth nearly $400 million in trade and investment with regional and international companies. The agreements were finalized during a business matchmaking event in Kabul, involving participants from Uzbekistan, India, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Almaty City Council Approves General Plan Draft Until 2040
item.description: The Almaty City Council has approved a draft amendment to the city's general plan until 2040. The document, which aligns residential development with infrastructure, will now be submitted to the government for final approval. The plan anticipates a population of 3.6 million by 2040.

item.title: Afghanistan Ranks Third Globally in Unexploded Ordnance Deaths, UNAMA Warns
item.description: Afghanistan ranks third worldwide in fatalities from unexploded ordnance, with large areas contaminated by war remnants, UNAMA has warned. Children are particularly vulnerable, making up 80% of casualties, often from playing with explosive devices. UNAMA urges public awareness and reporting of suspicious objects to prevent further deaths and calls for sustained mine-clearance support.

item.title: Kazakhstan Meets Only 66% of Prosthetic and Orthopedic Aid Needs for People with Disabilities
item.description: Kazakhstan has met only 66.1% of the demand for prosthetic and orthopedic aid for people with disabilities as of October 1st. Overall, 80.6% of rehabilitation needs were met. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection reported a slight increase in fulfillment rates compared to the previous year, highlighting ongoing efforts to improve support.

item.title: Pakistan Army: 12 TTP and Afghan Taliban members killed in border areas
item.description: The Pakistan Army reported that 12 members of the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and Afghan Taliban were killed in operations in border regions. The statement did not provide specific details on the timing or location of these operations.

item.title: Tajik Embassy in UK Invites Interested Individuals to Learn Tajik Language Online
item.description: The Tajik Embassy in London has announced an online Tajik language course for children of compatriots living in the UK and other interested individuals. Classes will be held twice a week. Interested parties must register by October 20, providing their name, age, and proficiency level.

item.title: Foreigner Detained for 15 Days in Almaty for Groping Woman in Park
item.description: A foreign national has been administratively detained for 15 days in Almaty for inappropriately touching a woman in Terrenkur Park. The individual, identified as a tourist who arrived in Kazakhstan the day before, was apprehended by local police. Authorities are reviewing his further stay in the country.

item.title: Houthi attack on Riyadh airport kills at least 12, injures hundreds
item.description: Yemeni Houthis launched a missile attack on Riyadh International Airport, killing at least 12 people and injuring approximately 400. This marks the third attack on the airport this week, and the most severe. Casualties included citizens from the US, Bangladesh, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt, in addition to Saudi nationals. The airport has temporarily closed.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Houthi Attack on Saudi Arabian Capital's Airport
item.description: The Uzbek Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed deep sorrow and strongly condemned the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The strike resulted in at least 12 deaths and approximately 310 injuries, including citizens of Saudi Arabia and the US. Uzbekistan reaffirmed its support for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and security.

item.title: Police Open Criminal Case After Stampede at Kairat Nurtas Concert Injures Teenager
item.description: Police have opened a criminal case following a stampede at a Kairat Nurtas concert in Shymkent that critically injured an 18-year-old girl. Relatives reported the girl was trampled by the crowd. Organizers have been taken to the police, and the investigation is ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident.

item.title: Carbon Monoxide Detectors to Be Installed for Large Families in Kyzylorda Region
item.description: 150 carbon monoxide detectors will be installed in the homes of large families in difficult socio-economic situations in the Kyzylorda region. The devices, purchased with sponsorship, detect dangerous gas concentrations and alert residents. This initiative is part of preventive measures for the heating season to prevent fires and poisoning.

item.title: Uzbekistan Condemns Attack on Riyadh International Airport, Calls for De-escalation
item.description: Uzbekistan has strongly condemned the attack on the international airport in Riyadh. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged an immediate cessation of such attacks, called for all parties to show restraint, and to prevent further escalation of tensions. The statement was released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes New CIS Cooperation Strategy for Next 35 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has proposed a new strategy for the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) development until 2035, focusing on economic, infrastructure, and technological projects. President Tokayev suggested forming a portfolio of flagship industrial-technological projects and strengthening transport connectivity. Kazakhstan also advocates for expanding CIS international cooperation through a 'CIS Plus' format.

item.title: Houthis Warn Airlines to Avoid Saudi Airports After Deadly Riyadh Attack
item.description: Yemen's Houthi movement has warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi airports and airspace, declaring them potential targets following a deadly attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport. The warning excluded Mecca and Medina. Saudi authorities reported 12 fatalities, including citizens from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.

item.title: Houthis Attack Saudi Arabia's Capital Airport, Causing Casualties
item.description: The airport in Saudi Arabia's capital was attacked by Houthis, resulting in 12 fatalities and over 300 injuries. This incident follows claims by the Houthis of striking the airport. The General Authority of Civil Aviation temporarily suspended airport operations for damage assessment and security checks. Official Saudi sources indicated that missiles hit terminals three and four.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Airport Leaves 12 Dead, Over 300 Injured, State Media Reports
item.description: An attack by Houthis on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh resulted in 12 deaths and 309 injuries, according to Egemen.kz. The report states the incident occurred days after the Houthis claimed responsibility for an airport strike. Saudi official sources cited by The Wall Street Journal indicated missiles hit terminals three and four, causing significant damage.

item.title: Trump Agrees to Buy Russian Diesel After Criticizing Ukraine's Attacks on Oil Refineries
item.description: Donald Trump criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky for attacks on Russian oil refineries, suggesting Ukraine needs a new leader capable of making peace. Trump stated he agreed to purchase diesel fuel from Russia after speaking with Vladimir Putin. Zelensky viewed this as enabling Russia's continued war efforts. US officials reportedly warned Ukraine to cease attacks on Russian refineries.

item.title: Yandex Services Experience Disruptions in Kazakhstan Following Drone Attacks
item.description: Yandex Go services, including taxi and food delivery, are experiencing disruptions in Kazakhstan. The company confirmed technical issues are affecting operations and is working on restoration, but timelines remain uncertain. Users report inability to book rides, impacting daily plans and courier work. Yandex cited distributed infrastructure for service operation.

item.title: Yandex Services Malfunction in Kazakhstan After Drone Attack on Data Centers
item.description: Following a drone attack on Yandex data centers in Russia, several Yandex services malfunctioned in Kazakhstan on Sunday, October 11. Yandex Go Kazakhstan confirmed technical issues causing temporary disruptions and apologized for the inconvenience. The company stated specialists are working to restore services as quickly as possible.

item.title: Yandex Services Cease Operations in Kazakhstan, Leaving Drivers and Couriers Unemployed
item.description: Yandex services, including taxi and delivery, have stopped working in Kazakhstan. This halt has left numerous drivers and couriers without work. The company has acknowledged the disruptions and is reportedly working on restoring services, but specific timelines for resumption remain unclear.
